title: A prime model without countable saturation: naming every rational
summary: Name every rational point to obtain a countable prime model whose theory has continuum many one-types and admits no countable saturated or elementary-universal model.
abstract: A constant naming each rational number forces every elementary embedding to keep track of every old rational point. This makes the named rational order a particularly rigid prime model: its embedding into any model of the same theory is uniquely determined. Yet it still leaves a simple request unanswered, asking for a point above every rational name. We compare this model with the real order carrying the same names. Rational cuts distinguish continuum many complete descriptions of a point, although the isolated descriptions pick out just the named rational points. The theory therefore has a countable prime model and no countable saturated or elementary-universal model.
